items.title: S&P Dow Jones Indices CEO on Index Restructuring
items.summary: Catherine Clay, CEO of S&P Dow Jones Indices, discusses the upcoming S&P reconstitution and rebalance, noting that the process is fully transparent and routine. She says market participants already know which names are entering and leaving the index, including Bloom Energy, Illumina and Everpure joining the S&P this month, and have ample time to adjust portfolios accordingly. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Tyler Kendall on "The Close."

items.title: What CRM Shareholders Got Paid While The Stock Stood Still
items.summary: The company sent owners a fortune in cash, yet the stock went backward. Here is the accounting on what that trade-off actually bought, and what it means now.

items.title: Is Joby Stock Priced For The Wrong Business?
items.summary: Joby Aviation (JOBY) stock has fallen 49.2% over the trailing twelve months to about $6.84, about 65% below its 52-week high. The shares change hands at 57.0 times sales, against 3.2 for the S&P 500. That multiple is accurate. It also measures a passenger brokerage business that represents a transitional step rather than the long-term eVTOL manufacturing thesis driving the stock's valuation.

items.title: Why Does AT&T Stock Still Trade Like It Is Shrinking?
items.summary: AT&T (T) trades at 8.2 times earnings against an S&P 500 median of 23.0, and it got there the hard way: the stock returned -9.4% over the past year while the index returned +19.3%. A profitable telecom throwing off cash at that discount is what value buyers hunt for.

items.title: How Far Could RKLB Stock Fall In The Next Shock?
items.summary: Rocket Lab (RKLB) trades near $64, about 57% below the high it set inside the last year, though it is still up 49.5% over twelve months against 19.7% for the S&P 500. The business did not break along the way. What changed is the wait: how long before Neutron flies, and how much cash goes out first.
